messages:
Natalie (Support): FYI customer Acme getting a 400 from /v1/rerank. They sent a payload we accepted but server returns generic "invalid request payload". Can someone help repro?

Devon (Backend): Can you paste the exact request body they sent (redact tokens)? 400 with vague message usually means a shape/type mismatch in the JSON.

Natalie (Support): Copied from the ticket (removed PII):
```json
{
  "queries": [ { "text": "Which is cheaper?" } ],
  "candidates": [ { "text": "Option A" }, null, { "text": "Option C" } ]
}
```
They claim they always used our SDK but switched to their own client for a batch test. Response body: `{"error":"invalid request payload"}` and 400.

Devon (Backend): Ah — our rerank schema requires each query to have an `id` and `text` (id is used for result mapping). Candidates must be objects with `id` and `text` as well; nulls not allowed. Our server currently fails schema validation in middleware and emits the generic 400.

Kevin (Integrations): We see this pattern with customers rolling their own wrappers. Suggestion: short-term we can improve the error payload to include a JSON pointer like "/candidates/1" and a reason `null candidate` so troubleshooters and clients can auto-fix. Long-term: add client-side validation into the JS/py SDKs.

Devon (Backend): Agree. Quick repro locally: curl to the internal staging endpoint with the sample body returns 400 and a stacktrace in logs. Repro steps:
```bash
curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"queries":[{"text":"Which is cheaper?"}],"candidates":[{"text":"Option A"},null,{"text":"Option C"}]}' -v
```
Expected server should return 400 with a helpful error. Current server: 400 `{"error":"invalid request payload"}`.

ops-bot: Log entry created: request_id=asf12-98, route=/v1/rerank, status=400, backend=rerank-validator, latency_ms=18

Devon (Backend): Quick fix plan: 1) change validator to emit structured error: `{"error":"bad_request","details":[{"path":"/candidates/1","msg":"candidate is null"}]}`. 2) add a 1-line check to the public SDKs to pre-validate arrays so users get early errors. 3) add an integration test case that includes nulls, missing ids, and non-string ids.

Natalie (Support): I pinged Acme to confirm their diff between successful and failing payloads and to ask for the request_id header (they provided request_id=asf12-98). I'll update the ticket when we have a fix or a workaround.

Kevin (Integrations): Also add a note to the support KB: "Rerank 400 — common causes" listing missing `id` fields, null candidates, candidates as plain strings (we expect objects), and empty `queries` arrays. Might avoid repeats.

acme_oncall: Thanks — we were surprised because our old client allowed arrays of strings for candidates. Is switching to objects breaking behavior? We can reformat on our side if you confirm expected schema.

Devon (Backend): Confirmed: we require objects with `id` and `text`. We accept candidate string shorthand in older legacy versions but that was removed in v2 because we need stable IDs for tie-breaking. We'll document that in the KB.

Natalie (Support): Action items: Devon -> server change (structured error) and add test (ETA 24h). Kevin -> docs KB update + SDK check (ETA 3 days). I'll send Acme the temporary workaround: map their string candidates to objects with generated ids and ensure no nulls.

Devon (Backend): I'll open a PR and include the failed-case payload in tests. Will tag @Kevin for SDK changes.

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered: PR #3421 -> staging (rerank-validator-improve-errors). CI status: running.

Natalie (Support): Thanks team. Keeping this thread open until PR merges and customer confirms the workaround works. :thumbsup:
